claim: American author and lawyer Ingersoll Lockwood (1841-1918) published two children's adventure novels — "Travels and Adventures of Little Baron Trump and his Wonderful Dog Bulger" (1889) and "Baron Trump's Marvellous Underground Journey" (1893) — whose German-boy protagonist Wilhelm Heinrich Sebastian Von Troomp goes by "Baron Trump." Three years after the second Baron Trump book, in 1896, Lockwood separately published "1900: or; The Last President," a dystopian short novel in which New York City is convulsed by protests after a populist outsider wins the 1896 presidential election and brings the United States toward collapse. The three works remained obscure until 2017, when they were widely re-circulated for perceived parallels with U.S. President Donald J. Trump.

sources.label: Newsweek — "Did an Author From the 1800s Predict the Trumps, Russia and America's Downfall?" August 25, 2017.
Sky HISTORY — "Ingersoll Lockwood: The author who predicted Trump's presidency."

notes: The three books exist and are in the historical record. The Baron Trump series is two books (1889, 1893), not three; "The Last President" (1896) is a SEPARATE Lockwood work that the @trueearth911 reel conflates as the trilogy's third volume. The reel's further claims — that Lockwood lived on the same street as Tesla, that the books predicted modern Trump events with named characters, etc. — are not asserted by this record. Record documents only the existence and content of the three Lockwood works.
